name: Essence Flux

abilities.text: Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control. If it's a Spirit, put a +1/+1 counter on it.

notes: APPROXIMATION, and the closest this vocabulary reaches: no condition asks whether a BOUND OBJECT ('that', the card just returned) has a subtype - the core conditions are about the source, the board or a player - so 'If it's a Spirit' is written as 'if you control a Spirit', evaluated after the return. It is exact whenever you control no other Spirit (the blinked Spirit is on the battlefield by then, and a blinked non-Spirit gets no counter unless another Spirit of yours is out); it over-counts only when you already control a Spirit and blink something else. The unconditional counter the previous draft put on every returned creature was rejected by both judges. See needs: a Ref-scoped condition { kind: 'ref-is', ref: Ref, filter: Filter } would make this exact (CR 608.2a).

issues: If it's a Spirit, put a +1/+1 counter on it. — expected The condition asks whether the RETURNED object (the new object created by the return, CR 400.7/608.2a) is a Spirit. Blink a non-Spirit -> no counter, always. — scripted conditional {kind:'controls', who:'you', filter:{subtypes:['Spirit']}, atLeast:1} then counters on 'that'. This is a different question: it is true whenever you control ANY Spirit. Blinking a non-Spirit while you control a Spirit token (the card's own deck archetype) puts a +1/+1 counter on the non-Spirit — a false positive that is easy to reach, not a corner case. No false negatives. — CR CR 400.7, 608.2a

Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control. — expected If the targeted creature is owned by an opponent (you control it via a control-change effect), it returns under the OPPONENT's control, and 'if it's a Spirit' still applies to it. — scripted return-to-battlefield target 'that' underControlOf 'owner' is correct for the return. The Spirit clause then misfires the other way in this case: the script asks whether YOU control a Spirit, so an opponent-owned Spirit returned under their control gets no counter unless you happen to control a Spirit of your own. — CR CR 110.2a

(process) notes cite a vocabulary need but none is filed — expected An approximation this consequential should carry an openNeeds entry (the notes themselves propose { kind:'ref-is', ref, filter }). — scripted batch card openNeeds is []; needs.json is a generated report and contains no entry for 64824ae5. I confirmed the schema (src/cards/schema-core.ts:487-548) has no ref-scoped condition, so the approximation really is the closest reachable today — but it is untracked.

If it's a Spirit, put a +1/+1 counter on it. — expected The counter is put on the returned permanent only if THAT permanent is a Spirit (CR 608.2a, an intervening test on the object itself). — scripted conditional {kind:'controls', who:'you', filter:{subtypes:['Spirit']}, atLeast:1} then counters on 'that'. characteristics.ts:429 tests your whole battlefield, so blinking a NON-Spirit while you control any other Spirit wrongly gives the blinked creature a +1/+1 counter - a common line in the Spirit deck this card is printed for. No scenario covers it (all four blind scenarios have a single relevant creature). The gap is real: no core condition tests a bound Ref's characteristics, and counters' own `filter` is only honoured for target 'creatures-you-control' (game.ts:1390), so it cannot rescue target 'that'. — CR CR 608.2a / 400.7

Exile target creature you control, then return that card to the battlefield under its owner's control. — expected Blink your own creature; it returns as a new object under its owner's control, counters and attachments gone. — scripted exile {kind:'creature', controller:'you'} then return-to-battlefield {target:'that', underControlOf:'owner'} (game.ts:1292 takes item.affected still in exile and enters it under o.owner). Correct. — CR CR 400.7 / 110.5
